newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HERZOG'S REVENGE KNOCKS BAYERN OFF THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HERZOG'S REVENGE KNOCKS BAYERN OFF THE TOP.

text.p: Midfielder Andreas Herzog took sweet revenge on his former team mates at Bayern Munich on Saturday, scoring twice in Werder Bremen's 3-0 win to knock the 13 times champions off the top of the German league.

Challengers VfB Stuttgart seized their chance to go first with alacrity, returning to their stylish winning ways with a 5-2 away win over Bayern's local rivals 1860 Munich featuring two goals from Brazilian Giovane Elber.
For Bayern, the stinging defeat came on top of a midweek defeat to Valencia in the first round of the UEFA Cup and a bout of public wrangling over the form of striker Juergen Klinsmann.

Austrian international Herzog opened the scoring with a 23rd minute penalty and struck his second two minutes after the interval. Another Bayern reject, Bruno Labbadia, made it three 20 minutes from time.

Herzog felt he had been badly treated in Munich, where he spent just one unhappy season before returning to Bremen in a swap for Mario Basler, and warned his former team mates before the match that he had "saved a little bit of anger for Bayern".
Herzog was jubilant after handing Bayern their first defeat of the season and pushing them down to third place.
"I showed them I can still play football," he said.

The result was especially galling for Basler, who told Bremen coach Dixie Doerner before the match: "I can only laugh when I hear that Bremen don't miss me... If I were still there, you'd be challenging at the top and playing for the title."
In the event Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni pulled Basler off at half time along with the out-of-sorts Klinsmann.
But Klinsmann at least could take consolation from national trainer Berti Vogts, who told the daily Bild:

"He's not out of form, he's just going through what all strikers go through...If (Bayern president) Franz Beckenbauer starts thinking out loud about resting him, I say, he needs confidence, and he won't get that on the bench...If he said he wanted to go, 20 clubs would be queueing up for him."
Meanwhile, Stuttgart set out to prove that they could still turn on the style now that young stand-in coach Joachim Loew has been given a full-time contract.

Last week Fortuna Duesseldorf spoiled Loew's party by handing the 1992 champions their first defeat of the season, and 1860 Munich looked like doing the same when Bernhard Winkler stabbed in a rebound from an Abedi Pele shot in the 11th minute.
But this time the southerners regained their composure as Elber and Matthias Hagner scored twice in two minutes.
In the 58th minute, Elber notched his fifth goal of the season, using the outside of his foot to sweep an unstoppable long-range shot past goalkeeper Rainer Berg.
Croatian international Zvonimir Soldo made it four in the 63rd minute and Fredi Bobic, last season's leading scorer, completed the rout six minutes later.
Ghana's Pele scored his first goal for 1860 Munich one minute from time to make the score 5-2.
Early-season pacesetters Bayer Leverkusen moved into second place on 18 points, one behind Stuttgart and one ahead of Bayern, with a 2-1 win at Schalke.
Last season's champions Borussia Dortmund are seventh with 13 points, but entertain lowly St Pauli on Sunday.
In the day's other matches, Freiburg recorded their first win of the season by beating Hansa Rostock 1-0.
Hamburg and Duisburg drew 1-1, and Borussia Moenchengladbach came back down to earth after putting Arsenal out of the UEFA Cup, losing 1-0 at local rivals Duesseldorf.
